newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Heavy call buying in FORE Systems.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Heavy call buying in FORE Systems.

text.p: Call buying was heavy in FORE Systems Inc as the stock held up well in the face of a broad market selloff.
In late trading, shares of the company were off 1/4 at 15-13/16 on more than five million shares.

"Yesterday and today we've had excessive option volume," said a market maker in Chicago. "Mostly buyers of calls and that's taken the volatility from the low 70's to the high 80's, low 90's on a lot of speculation."
He said FORE has been the subject of takeover rumors in the past but he had not heard of any such talk this week.
An options trader at the Pacific Exchange said investors were mainly buying the September 15 and September 17-1/2 calls.

"It's coming from five lots to 200 and 300 lots," he said, adding that some put buying was also seen, but on a smaller scale. In addition, one institution was a seller of puts at the 15 strike level, he said.
The September 17-1/2 calls were the most active, with turnover of more than 5,000 contracts. Open interest through Thursday was just 572 contracts.
The September 15 calls, which had open interest of 1,627 contracts, traded about 2,700 contracts.
The most active August call was the 15, which traded about 2,040 contracts. That option expires in two weeks.
Among FORE puts, the September 15 traded 855 contracts and the August 15 traded about 800.
FORE options trade on all four options exchanges.

The trader at the Pacific Exchange said most investors expected the stock to fall after the company said Thursday that a revenue forecast given on Wednesday by an employee on Asian revenues should be disregarded.

"Everybody assumed the stock would be down," the options trader said. "It went down at the open on short speculation, but it was so strong, there were large institutional bids. When the stock turned, the call buyers just came in like we haven't seen in a couple months."
FORE shares hit a session low of 15-1/4 in the first few minutes of trading.
Regarding the options activity, the trader said: "Something's up, but what it is, who knows."
